xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3254: Review/test pipeline re-drove one issue 426 times in 19.5 hours, every cycle reporting 'no code changed'

plan.title: Review/test pipeline re-drove one issue 426 times in 19.5 hours, every cycle reporting 'no code changed'
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: The post-review Deacon patrol reset MIN-901's review/test to pending 426 times in 19.5 hours because a polyrepo composite reviewedAtCommit anchor compared against a bare wrapper-HEAD snapshot was reported as drift before any content check, and the wrapper HEAD never moves. The fix (shape mismatch -> unreadable; polyrepo snapshot resolution by repoKey OR repoPath; refuse degraded wrapper-HEAD snapshots; repeat-reset bound with a one-time review-reset-loop needs-you escalation) already landed on main in fb99ed40fa with locking tests, and is an ancestor of this branch. The residual defect: docs/REVIEW-AGENT-ARCHITECTURE.md still documents the removed behavior — it claims a shape mismatch is 'intentionally reported as drift once' and says nothing about the repeat-reset bound or its operator-visible needs-you escalation.
narratives.Proposal: Correct docs/REVIEW-AGENT-ARCHITECTURE.md to match the shipped code: replace the stale 'drift once' paragraph with the unreadable-on-shape-mismatch semantics, document the repeat-reset bound (one reset per distinct anchor, then suppress + one review-reset-loop needs-you, process-local state, new anchor still resets), cite the MIN-901 426-cycle incident as the motivating failure, and name the locking test files. Documentation-only branch diff.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No changes to src/lib/cloister/deacon-post-review-commits.ts, src/lib/workspace-anchor-drift.ts, src/lib/project-repos.ts, or src/lib/git-utils.ts — the fix already landed in fb99ed40fa and must not be re-implemented or extended
- No persistence of the repeat-reset bound's in-memory state across dashboard restarts (accepted backstop; worst post-restart cost is one extra reset)
- No changes to the PAN-3151 review convergence gate (it targets non-converging blocking findings, a different failure mode)
- No event-payload capping or storage remediation (that is PAN-3253)
- No live/deploy verification that MIN-891/902/858 stopped churning — deploy and verify-on-main are owned by close-out per the Definition of Done, not this branch

autoDecisions.summary: Scoped this issue's remaining work to documentation only, without asking the operator.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue comment states the fix landed on main in fb99ed40fa (operator-directed, gates green); git confirms it is an ancestor of feature/pan-3254, and its tests map 1:1 onto all three issue acceptance criteria (shape-mismatch->unreadable; reset-once-then-suppress-then-escalate replaying the MIN-901 signature; new-anchor-still-resets). The only artifact the fix left stale is docs/REVIEW-AGENT-ARCHITECTURE.md, which now contradicts shipped behavior.

autoDecisions.summary: Chose docs/REVIEW-AGENT-ARCHITECTURE.md as the sole documentation target.
autoDecisions.rationale: It is the only file containing a now-false claim ('intentionally reported as drift once'). CLAUDE.md's pipeline sections do not describe anchor-drift semantics, so duplicating there would create drift risk without adding a surface operators actually consult for this behavior.

autoDecisions.summary: Documented (rather than persisted) the process-local repeat-reset bound state.
autoDecisions.rationale: The primary loop driver is eliminated at the drift-evaluator layer, making the bound a backstop; persisting its Maps would add a storage surface for a one-extra-reset-after-restart edge the issue does not require closing.

items.title: Correct anchor-drift and repeat-reset-bound documentation in REVIEW-AGENT-ARCHITECTURE.md

verify_commands: grep -c 'reported as drift once' docs/REVIEW-AGENT-ARCHITECTURE.md; test $? -eq 1
expected_outputs: grep for 'review-reset-loop' prints a count of at least 1
grep for 'reported as drift once' finds zero matches (exits 1)

narrative.Action: In docs/REVIEW-AGENT-ARCHITECTURE.md, locate by phrase search (not line number) the paragraph beginning 'A legacy wrapper SHA compared with a current composite anchor is intentionally reported as drift once.' Replace it with the shipped PAN-3254 semantics: a composite/bare anchor SHAPE disagreement is a producer disagreement, not code change — evaluateWorkspaceAnchorDrift() returns unreadable, callers skip, and the existing verdict is preserved; a genuine post-review push differs by content in a well-formed anchor. Recount the motivating failure as MIN-901's 426 identical review cycles in 19.5 h (the wrapper HEAD never moves), keeping the still-true sentence about logs rendering every token as repoKey@<8-char sha>. Then extend the numbered checkPostReviewCommits() site description with the repeat-reset bound: the patrol records the current anchor at each reset; a second drifted verdict against the same anchor is suppressed and escalates one review-reset-loop needs-you via recordDeadEndNeedsYou instead of looping; a genuinely new anchor still resets; bound state is process-local in-memory, cleared when the issue merges and on dashboard restart. Name the locking tests: tests/unit/lib/workspace-anchor-drift.test.ts (shape mismatch -> unreadable) and tests/unit/lib/cloister/deacon-post-blocked-review-commits.test.ts (reset-once-then-suppress-then-escalate; new-anchor-still-resets). Touch no other file.
narrative.Why: The doc describes the exact mechanism ('drift once, then stabilize') that failed to stabilize and was removed by fb99ed40fa; anyone debugging a future reset loop from this doc would be steered to the superseded model, and the operator-visible review-reset-loop needs-you escalation is currently undocumented.

The shape-mismatch paragraph states the evaluator returns unreadable and preserves the existing verdict, citing PAN-3254 and the MIN-901 426-cycle incident
The checkPostReviewCommits() site description states a repeated drifted verdict against the same anchor is suppressed and emits one review-reset-loop needs-you, while a new anchor still resets review
The doc contains both locking test file paths, and git diff origin/main --stat shows docs/REVIEW-AGENT-ARCHITECTURE.md as the only non-planning-artifact change
